pairs.locus: De Ente et Essentia, cap. IV
pairs.question: Utrum ista natura sic considerata possit dici una vel plures?
pairs.answer: Neutrum concedendum est, quia utrumque est extra intellectum humanitatis et utrumque potest sibi accidere.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical question and self-answer. Source: 'Unde si quaeratur utrum ista natura sic considerata possit dici una vel plures, neutrum concedendum est, quia utrumque est extra intellectum humanitatis et utrumque potest sibi accidere.' Dropped the asking-frame 'Unde si quaeratur' (narrates the posing of the question); capitalized 'Utrum' and added '?'. The answer runs from 'Neutrum' to the first full stop (the comma-joined causal clause is part of the same sentence); what follows ('Si enim pluralitas esset...') begins a new sentence elaborating the reasons, so it is cut. All other apparent interrogatives in the treatise are expository 'videndum est / restat videre / patet quod' statements, not posed-and-answered questions.
